newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended firm but below highs. Much of the action was focused on the September/November switch where the premium soared to a high of $101.00 a tonne before settling at $49.00 at the close. The November contract was up $11.00 at $1,545 per tonne.

In New York arabica futures ended weaker hurt by a late-session bout of speculative liquidation. Traders said December's failure to carve out fresh upside territory inspired a swift round of speculative selling ahead of the close.

However, one problem is transportation in Colombia with possible delays due to trucker protests and rebel guerilla activity. But traders said this is something that comes up periodically and is probably discounted to a large degree. Colombian coffee export shipments have been delayed for about three days due to the guerilla activity.

There has been some talk of a possible force majeure due to transportation problems but this is premature at this point, it was added. Given the anticipated surplus in 1996/97, traders still expect that the market will test the $1.00-barrier basis December.

UNITED STATES - Certified coffee stocks showed another marginal rise during the week ended September 6. Stocks in New York rose by 500 bags (+250 bags) to 4,811 bags (4,311 bags), while stocks in New Orleans fell by 1,146 bags (+2,000 bags) to 26,990 bags (28,136 bags). Stocks in San Francisco increased by 1,750 bags (+/-0) to 5,250 bags (3,500 bags) while stocks in Miami remained unchanged at 5,616 bags.

UNITED STATES - During the week ended August 31, coffee roastings totalled approximately 315,000 60-kg bags, down from 340,000 bags in the previous week and compared with 335,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 11.330 million bags versus 11.105 million bags in the same year-ago period.

ITALY - Italy imported 529,008 bags of coffee in March 1996, 6.4 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.543 million bags, 5.7 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 1.6 per cent to 5.387 million bags.

Major suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1996 were Zaire (148,100 vs 208,800 bags), Brazil (365,500 vs 421,800 bags), India (125,600 vs 113,300 bags) and Colombia (136,500 vs 87,600 bags). The country exported 193,200 bags of coffee in January/March 1996, 23 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 rose by 5.2 per cent to 738,900 bags.
